hints.title: Two-Pass Counting Elimination Obstacle
hints.text: Counting total nodes first requires two full passes over the list. How can two runners moving at different speeds pinpoint the exact predecessor of the middle node in a single pass?

hints.title: Sentinel Staggered Fast-Slow Invariant
hints.text: Advance fast by two steps and slow by one step starting with slow at a sentinel dummy node so slow halts immediately before the middle node.

hints.title: Middle Node Bypassing Procedure
hints.text: If head.next is null, return null. Initialize dummy pointing to head, with slow at dummy and fast at head. While fast and fast.next exist, advance slow by one and fast by two. Skip the middle node by setting slow.next to slow.next.next. Return dummy.next.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def deleteMiddle(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return None
        dummy = ListNode(0, head)
        slow = dummy
        fast = head
        while fast and fast.next:
            slow = slow.next
            fast = fast.next.next
        slow.next = slow.next.next
        return dummy.next
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single pass fast and slow pointer traversal stopping at the middle predecessor.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Length counting requires traversing the list twice, which increases cache misses compared to a single pass.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Staggering fast and slow from a dummy sentinel locates the predecessor in O(1) space in a single pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling the base case of a single node list returning null cleanly.
